You are doing functional research for "Atlas ERP", an open-source ERP whose explicit benchmark is SAP S/4HANA. Your assigned S/4HANA area: Sales & Distribution (SD).

TASK: Establish what this area actually covers in current S/4HANA (2025/2026), identify the 6-12 capabilities practitioners consider essential, and judge each against the planned Atlas v1 scope below.

METHOD: Use WebSearch (and WebFetch for promising pages) - 2 to 5 targeted searches. Prefer SAP Help Portal, SAP Community, and reputable ERP consulting sources. If web tools are unavailable or consistently fail, fall back to your embedded knowledge of S/4HANA and say so explicitly in the overview field.

COVER AT MINIMUM: Customer master, pricing & condition technique, sales orders, available-to-promise (ATP), shipping and deliveries, billing, credit management, returns processing.

PLANNED ATLAS V1 SCOPE FOR THIS AREA (judge full/partial/out-of-scope against THIS, not your own ideas):
Customer master; condition-style pricing (price lists per currency / customer group / date range, discounts); Quote -> Order -> Delivery -> Invoice with partial shipments and backorders; simple ATP check against on-hand + on-order; credit-limit block at order confirmation; RMA returns with credit notes.

RULES:
- atlas_v1 = "full" when Atlas v1 plans the practitioner-essential core of the capability; "partial" when a meaningful but reduced subset is planned; "out-of-scope" when none of it is planned.
- Every "partial" and "out-of-scope" entry MUST have a non-empty reason (why cut / where the boundary sits) and later_path (how to add it later in one line).
- atlas_module must be one of: finance, inventory, procurement, sales, manufacturing, quality, maintenance, hr, projects, crm, reporting, admin, industry, core, frontend, or "-" for out-of-scope.
- Be honest: if S/4HANA has an essential capability the Atlas plan misses entirely, include it as out-of-scope rather than omitting it.

Your final output is consumed by a script - return only the structured data.

## Order-to-Cash & Pricing

SAP S/4HANA enables faster order-to-cash cycles with reduced data latency. Sales managers can view the order-to-cash cycle time or sales-related data in an instant. I've completed a web search on SAP S/4HANA Sales and Distribution modules with a focus on advanced ATP (aATP), condition technique, and business partner functionality. Here's an overview of the key findings:

## S/4HANA Sales and Distribution Overview

The transformation from SAP ECC to S/4HANA has changed how business operations are handled in the Sales and Distribution module, utilizing the in-memory database structure with simplified data models and user-friendly interfaces.

## Advanced Available-to-Promise (aATP)

Advanced Available-to-Promise (aATP) is a critical component of the S/4HANA suite that enhances the standard ATP functionality with more advanced and flexible features, designed to meet complex order fulfillment processes and ensure higher accuracy and efficiency in inventory allocation and customer order management.

Advanced ATP provides accurate and reliable order promise dates that consider the relevant supplies across the network and critical supply chain constraints in real time, such as inventory positioning, transportation, production, and procurement.

### Key aATP Features:

aATP includes Product Allocation Lists (PAL), product availability checks (PAC), supply protection (SUP), alternative-based confirmation (ABC), backorder processing (BOP), supply assignment (ARun), and supply creation-based confirmation (SBC).

In contrast to the ECC solution, aATP can be used to allocate both before and after the product availability check, such as customer-based quota allocation before the ATP check and capacity quota allocation after the ATP check.

## Business Partner Approach

S/4HANA introduces the Business Partner method where one business partner can have multiple roles (such as Sold-To, Ship-To, Payer).

S/4HANA makes billing processes in SD more efficient with the Business Partner approach, which is a substitute for the classical customer master data record.

## Condition Technique

Configuration of the condition contract includes condition tables to contract types.

content.content:
# Key Functional Capabilities of SAP S/4HANA Sales

**Data Model Simplification**
Eliminates redundant status and index tables, consolidating fields into header and item tables. This reduces memory footprint and improves query performance while lowering total cost of ownership.

**Sales Order Fulfillment Cockpit**
Provides unified visibility into order-to-cash processes through a "single dashboard" where sales representatives can identify and resolve issues across sales, delivery, supply chain, and billing categories.

**Advanced Intercompany Sales**
Automates end-to-end transactions between company entities, automatically generating corresponding purchase orders, sales orders, and invoices while maintaining financial transparency and optimizing inventory synchronization.

**Valuated Stock-in-Transit (VSiT)**
Enables selling goods in transit between locations with precise valuation, allowing revenue recognition based on control transfer dates per IFRS 15 requirements.

**Pricing Management**
Supports workflow-based price approvals for orders exceeding thresholds, condition maintenance with upper/lower limits, tax rate management, and omnichannel promotion integration through SAP Omnichannel Promotion Pricing.

**Condition Contract Settlement**
Replaces traditional SD rebates with flexible, rule-based settlement processes offering high performance and innovative scenarios without requiring redundant database tables.

**Advanced Returns Management**
Handles warehouse returns, counter returns, and direct vendor shipments while supporting third-party product returns, customer-site inspections, and flexible refund timing.

**Billing Enhancements**
Includes preliminary billing functionality, down payment processing tied to milestone billing plans, recurring billing with rule-based scheduling, and billing document split analysis.

**Credit Management and Revenue Accounting**
Utilizes SAP Credit Management (replacing SD credit functions) and SAP Revenue Accounting and Reporting for IFRS 15 compliance, with data migration tools provided.

**Foreign Trade Management**
Provides import/export management functionalities and Intrastat reporting capabilities, though legal/export controls now use international trade-based approaches rather than material master fields.

**Analytics and Monitoring**
Delivers SAP Fiori apps including sales performance prediction, KPI dashboards integrated with SAP Analytics Cloud, AI-powered copilot features (Joule), and collaborative tools for issue resolution.

Based on your search results, here's an overview of the key SAP S/4HANA SD essential processes you asked about:

## Sales Order
When you create a sales order in response to a customer requirement, the system checks for the availability of goods and creates delivery proposals. A Sales Order is a legal document that captures a customer's request to purchase goods or services under agreed conditions and becomes the single source of truth for logistics, finance, and billing.

## Delivery & Post Goods Issue
The outbound delivery forms the basis of goods issue posting. The data required for goods issue posting is copied from the outbound delivery into the goods issue document, which cannot be changed manually. Any changes must be made in the outbound delivery itself, ensuring the goods issue document is an accurate reflection of the outbound delivery.

## Billing Document
The billing document is created by referencing the outbound delivery (for goods) or the sales order (for services). Billing creates a billing document using data from the sales order and the delivery document, with billing data (Revenue) transferred to FI and—if applicable—to the sales order item.

## Advanced Returns Management
Advanced Returns Management (ARM) is a long process that can be divided into process and configuration parts, with the process at an overview scope. The basic ARM steps include: Step 1 - creation of ARM (VA01), Step 2 - PGR Receipt of Return Material, Step 3 - Inspection Material, Step 4 - Refund Determination and Create Credit Memo Request.

## Credit Check Overview
Credit management integration ensures customer credit limits are checked in real time during sales order processing to prevent financial risk. However, there is no credit check that takes place in the GI posting process.

capabilities.description: Condition-technique engine: pricing procedures, condition types (price, discount, surcharge, freight, tax), access sequences, scales, and approval workflows.
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 plans condition-style price lists by currency/customer group/date range plus discounts, but not the generalized access-sequence/pricing-procedure engine, quantity scales, freight/tax condition types, or price-approval workflows.
capabilities.later_path: Generalize price tables into condition tables with a pluggable access-sequence resolver and an ordered pricing procedure.

capabilities.description: Pre-sales quotation through sales order capture with document flow, copy control, statuses, and partial fulfillment tracking; the order is the single source of truth for logistics and billing.
Product availability check at order entry; aATP adds product allocation, alternative-based confirmation, supply protection, and mass backorder processing runs.
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 plans a simple check against on-hand plus on-order with manual backorders, but none of aATP: no product allocation/quotas, alternative plant/substitution confirmation, supply protection, or prioritized mass BOP runs.
capabilities.later_path: Add a scheduled re-promising (backorder run) job and allocation buckets on top of the existing availability query.

capabilities.description: Outbound delivery documents with shipping point/route determination, picking, packing/handling units, goods issue posting, and EWM/TM integration.
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 plans delivery documents with partial shipments and stock issue, but no picking/packing/handling units, shipping point or route determination, wave processing, or warehouse/transportation integration.
capabilities.later_path: Layer pick lists, packing/handling units, and shipping-point/route rules onto the delivery document later.

capabilities.description: Billing documents from deliveries or orders with FI revenue posting, plus collective billing, invoice splits, credit/debit memos, billing plans (milestone/periodic), and preliminary billing.
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 plans per-delivery invoicing with FI posting and credit notes, but not collective billing runs, invoice split/merge rules, milestone or recurring billing plans, or preliminary billing.
capabilities.later_path: Add a collective billing-due-list job with split/merge rules, then billing plans as a follow-on.

capabilities.description: FSCM-based credit management (replaces classic SD credit): credit segments, rules-based scoring, real-time exposure across orders/deliveries/AR, and documented credit decisions with release workflow.
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 plans only a static credit-limit block at order confirmation; no exposure aggregation across open orders/deliveries/receivables, no rechecks at delivery, and no scoring or release workbench.
capabilities.later_path: Introduce a finance-owned exposure ledger and a blocked-documents release queue, rechecking at delivery creation.

capabilities.description: Return orders with goods receipt back to stock and credit memos; ARM adds inspection codes, refund determination rules, and follow-up logistics such as return-to-vendor.
capabilities.later_path: Inspection dispositions, refund-determination rules, and vendor-return chains can be added on the RMA later.

capabilities.description: Long-term quantity/value contracts and scheduling agreements with release orders/delivery schedules drawn down against agreed limits.
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 covers only the quote -> order flow; no long-term agreement document types or release-order consumption against contracted quantities/values exist in the plan.
capabilities.later_path: Add a contract document type with copy control to orders and quantity/value drawdown tracking.

capabilities.capability: Output management (order confirmations, delivery notes, invoices)
capabilities.description: Rule-driven generation and dispatch of sales documents as print/PDF/email/EDI, with form templates per document type; strengthened again in the 2025 release.
capabilities.reason: The Atlas v1 sales plan defines transactional documents but says nothing about rendering or transmitting them to customers, which practitioners treat as mandatory for go-live.
capabilities.later_path: Add template-based PDF/email rendering keyed by document type and customer as a cross-module output service.

capabilities.description: Rule-based condition contract settlement (successor to classic SD rebates) for retroactive customer rebates and commercial settlements.
capabilities.reason: No rebate accruals or settlement against sales volumes are in the Atlas v1 plan; only immediate order-level discounts are covered.
capabilities.later_path: Build on the condition engine later: accrue per qualifying invoice and settle periodically via credit memo.

capabilities.description: Automated cross-company sales with paired purchase/sales orders and intercompany invoices, plus third-party orders where the vendor ships directly to the customer.
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 assumes a single selling entity shipping its own stock; no cross-company document pairing or vendor drop-ship triggering from sales orders is planned.
capabilities.later_path: Add order-triggered purchase requisitions (drop-ship) first, then paired intercompany order/invoice generation.

content.text: Done. The structured assessment of S/4HANA Sales & Distribution against the Atlas v1 scope has been returned: 12 capabilities total, with 2 judged full (sales order management, RMA returns), 6 partial (customer master, pricing, ATP, shipping, billing, credit management), and 4 out-of-scope (contracts/scheduling agreements, output management, rebates, intercompany/drop-ship), each with reasons and later paths. Findings were grounded in live web research from SAP Community, SAP PRESS, and SAP Help Portal sources.
